cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Calm About the Impossible
cards.instruction: Remain perfectly calm around impossible events while becoming increasingly alarmed by ordinary details.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your dragon can stay for tea. Please keep the biscuit crumbs off my carpet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His three heads breathe fire. Should I take him outside?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. He's fine here. Wait, three mouths? I need three napkins immediately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He brought his own. They're paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Paper? At my good table? Fetch the linen before the neighbors see.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides dragon admission, A3 refuses B2 proposed removal and assigns napkins, A5 commands linen; S01 directly controls the mundane alarm while calmly permitting fire.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 three fire-breathing heads causes A3 three napkins instead of removal; B4 paper napkins causes A5 linen requirement and social alarm.

relationship.evidence: B2 owner proposes taking a dangerous guest out; B4 offers the guest own napkins, a useful solution A evaluates through etiquette.

heightening.evidence: A5 escalates B4 provided paper napkins into alarm over neighbors, developing ordinary propriety rather than fear of dragon fire.

specificity.evidence: A1 tea, carpet and guest establish host roles; B2 owner fire warning makes the split between danger and mundane concern immediately playable.
